Full-stack developer and rapid prototyper (Python, Next.js, FastAPI, data pipelines). Experienced in building clean, functional MVPs and interactive web tools under tight hackathon deadlines. 

Looking for teammates with strengths in UI/UX design, scientific research/data analysis, or pitch deck storytelling to create a polished, high-impact submission. Let’s build something stellar!
summary: Outpost Zero: Mission Aurora is a Roblox game that teaches kids aged 7-15 how astronauts survive and work on the Moon and Mars. Players take the role of Commander Alex Morgan after a micrometeorite strike damages a lunar outpost. They realign solar panels, restart the generator, manage oxygen, CO2, water and food, shield the base from radiation, grow hydroponic crops, and talk to Mission Control through a realistic Earth-Moon radio delay. They then choose cargo, launch in the AURORA lander, and build a new base on Mars. There they clean dusty solar panels, start a Kilopower reactor and MOXIE oxygen plant, drill for ice water, survive a dust storm, and send the first report to Earth. Players also do field surveys, comparing rock observations like real scientists. Real NASA data, such as Moon and Mars gravity, drives the gameplay, and short NASA facts appear as the story unfolds. It is a free, colorful, hands-on way to learn about life support, power, and space exploration.
details:
WHAT IT DOES

Outpost Zero is a two-chapter story game that trains "junior astronauts" (ages 7-15) in the basics of living and working off Earth. Chapter 1 takes place at a Moon outpost near the lunar South Pole; Chapter 2 on Mars.

HOW IT WORKS

Players survive by watching live telemetry bars (oxygen, CO2, water, food, power, radiation, health) and completing objectives. Moon: align the solar array, restart the generator, choose a power-grid mode (balanced, life support, crops or communications), reinforce regolith radiation shielding, harvest hydroponic crops, transmit through the Deep Space Network, and complete a rock survey. Players then pick up to 3 cargo items that carry over to Mars. Mars: wipe dust off solar panels, deploy a Kilopower-style fission reactor, start a MOXIE-style oxygen plant, drill and melt subsurface ice, shelter during a dust storm, repair the antenna, and send the first report.

BENEFITS AND IMPACT

It turns real engineering trade-offs (power budgeting, closed-loop life support, radiation shielding, communication delay, resource use on-site) into game decisions, so kids learn by doing. Short NASA fact callouts appear at key moments, and a NASA DATA panel lists the sources. Failure screens explain WHY a crew member would fail (for example hypoxia or radiation), turning mistakes into lessons.

TOOLS USED

Roblox Studio with Luau scripting. Procedural 3D construction (habitat, lander, terrain, Mars base). Roblox MaterialService PBR textures. Creator Store music. AI assistance (Claude) helped write and debug code and draft text.

DESIGN CHOICES

We prioritised a clear story, short sessions (15-20 minutes), a compact HUD, quiet sound design, and readable objectives for young players. Some elements are stylized for gameplay: the lander flight, travel time, star visibility, and the compressed communication delay.
